LESSON: ACTIVE LISTENING NON-VERBAL COMMUNICATION ATTENTION VOCABULARY ACTIVE ENGAGEMENT

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Listening and speaking
Topic 1.4: Active Listening Non-verbal communication Attention Vocabulary Active engagement

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Active Listening Non-verbal communication Attention Vocabulary Active engagement. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How else do you communicate without speaking?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. demonstrate a willingness to be receptive to new ideas in oral interactions
2. demonstrate willingness to be receptive to new ideas in oral interactions
3. respond to questions and prompts to show comprehension and engagement

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT WORD READING MEANS
Word reading is looking at a written word and saying it correctly.
Some longer words do not follow simple letter–sound rules. Your teacher models them. You look, listen, then say.

METHODS TO STUDY
1. Look-and-say: see the whole word, hear it, say it, cover it, write it.
2. Chunking: split long words — foot+ball, class+room, sun+shine.
3. Root words: in “handmade”, see “hand” and “made”.
4. Word ladder: change one letter at a time (sun → run → ran) and read each step.

WEEKLY HABIT
Learn about 8–10 new longer words each week. Practise in a group, with a partner, and alone.

WORKED EXAMPLES
A: elephant — look, listen to the model, say “elephant”, write it.
B: football = foot + ball
C: Word ladder: cat → hat → hot → hop

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1 — Look and say: “elephant” together, then in pairs, then alone.

Example 2 — Chunking: classroom = class + room.

Example 3 — Word ladder: sun → run → ran.

Example 4 — Home: pick two long newspaper words; repeat after a parent; write them.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Read five long words from a chart while pointing under each word.
2. Build a four-step word ladder and read it aloud.
3. Chunk: football, classroom, sunshine, handmade.
4. Write three new words and use each in a school sentence.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Copy eight new longer words. Read them to a parent tonight.
2. Make one word ladder of at least four steps.
3. Answer: How do you read a word you have never seen before?

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How else do you communicate without speaking?
2. Why is paying attention important when listening?
3. Why should you not interrupt others when they are speaking?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Look at the whole word, then say it clearly.
2. Use chunks, roots, and look-and-say.
3. Practise about eight to ten new longer words each week.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
